summary: Build a viral "Will you be my Valentine?" website.
architectural_notes: Store and serve the two GIF assets from the frontend (e.g., under public/assets) and reference them directly in the UI.

Background audio should be implemented in a way that respects browser autoplay policies (likely starts after first user interaction) and should use a properly licensed/hosted audio asset rather than streaming directly from a YouTube link.
known_issues: Deployment may fail without a visible error message due to a temporary platform/backend timeout during compilation; retrying deploy often succeeds.

existing_features.title: Create a single-page interactive “Will you be my Valentine?” experience with a clear prompt, two primary actions (“Yes” and “No”), and delightful animations that work on both desktop and mobile.

Implement the viral interaction pattern: tapping/clicking “No” should progressively make “Yes” more compelling (e.g., increasing size, adding emphasis) and/or make “No” harder to click (e.g., playful movement), while remaining accessible and not breaking the layout.

When the user clicks “Yes”, transition to a celebration screen with a romantic confirmation message, celebratory animation (e.g., floating hearts/confetti), and a clear “Start over” control to replay the experience.

Add lightweight sharing support to encourage virality: include a “Share” button that uses the Web Share API when available, and otherwise provides a copy-to-clipboard fallback for the current page URL with a short, editable share message in English.

Apply a coherent, distinctive visual theme suitable for a playful Valentine micro-site (colors, typography, spacing, and motion) and enforce it consistently across all screens. Avoid default/plain styling.

Add generated static visual assets (illustrations/background) to support the theme, store them under frontend/public/assets/generated, and render them in the UI without routing image bytes through the backend.

Update the question (first) screen content order to: (1) show the text "Tannu" at the top, (2) display the first uploaded GIF "cat-love-you.gif" below it, and (3) show the prompt text "Will you be my valentine? 💕" below the GIF.
Adjust the "No" interaction behavior so that each click progressively scales the "No" button smaller and scales the "Yes" button larger (while keeping both usable and not breaking layout).

Update the celebration (after "Yes") screen to display, in order: (1) "Tannu", (2) the second uploaded GIF "hai.gif", (3) a large headline text exactly "Yay! You're my valentine 😘", and (4) a smaller line of text exactly "I knew you would say yes baby hehehehe".
Add the uploaded GIF files as static frontend assets and reference them via stable paths from the React UI (do not route image bytes through the backend).

Add continuous background music that plays throughout the entire Valentine experience (both the question and celebration stages) using the requested track reference: “glue song” by beabadoobee (sped up + pitched) from https://youtube.com/shorts/Zy02CEOqrR4?si=ULEbg8LDnjIwxoc3.

Serve the background music as a static frontend asset (do not stream from YouTube): add an audio file under the frontend public folder (e.g., frontend/public/assets/audio/glue-song-sped-up-pitched.mp3) and play it via a stable /assets/... URL from the React UI.
Add an accessible music control UI that allows the user to toggle background music on/off (mute/unmute) while preserving the current visual theme and layout (mobile + desktop).
Ensure background audio playback behavior is compatible with modern browser autoplay policies by requiring a user interaction to start playback when needed (without showing intrusive prompts).
